summary: Tested Priority 3's live-ride gate (Systemic Fatigue: HR drift >5% over 15min while power holds steady -> hydration protocol + target cap). Backend: existing regression suite test_iter112_struggle_and_debrief.py re-confirmed 4/4 PASS against the public preview URL. New test_iter118_systemic_fatigue.py (2/2 PASS) covers: POST /api/coach/cue cue_kind='struggle', struggle_reasons=['systemic_fatigue'], eased_pct=10 -> 200 with a valid, calm hydration cue (lexically checked it does NOT read like a 'push harder' cue) exercising the new instruction branch; and struggle_reasons=['power_fade'] (no systemic_fatigue) -> 200, unchanged generic struggle branch. Code review of struggle.ts confirms systemicFatigue() gate math matches spec exactly: 15-min longBuf (LONG_WINDOW_SEC), gated on >=13min of data (LONG_WINDOW_MIN_SEC), powerStable = |p2-p1|<=8% of p1, hrDrift = (h2-h1)/h1 > 0.05, standalone trigger (active = ... || reasons.includes('systemic_fatigue')), 10% ease (easePct = primary==='systemic_fatigue' ? 0.10 : ...), REASON_PRIORITY correctly orders it above hr_near_max/power_fade. workout.tsx onStruggle correctly branches on s.primary==='systemic_fatigue' for hydration-specific toast/log wording and passes remainingIntervalSec/age/systemic fields through unchanged. summary.tsx STRUGGLE_LABEL map has the new systemic_fatigue -> 'HR drift (hydration)' entry, code path reviewed and will not crash if present in ride data. Frontend: logged in as demo@roujaune.app, started 'Threshold Intervals' live workout -> HUD loaded, telemetry ticked (elapsed/calories/interval countdown), bc-erg testID present, End-ride dialog (Save Ride/Abandon/Resume) worked, Save Ride -> /summary rendered cleanly with no crash/red-screen (needsManual manual-entry card shown correctly since the short simulated session had <30 samples). As flagged in the review request, forcing the actual 13-15min sustained HR-drift-while-power-stable gate through simulated web-preview telemetry within a short automated test window was not achievable -- reported as untestable via current tooling, consistent with the prior two rounds' hardest-to-trigger gates (ERG spiral, pre-emptive W').

ui_bugs.issue: Starting the specific catalog workout 'Welcome Ride' (workoutId=ctr-ride-1, Endurance > Beginner) immediately (within 1-4 seconds of elapsed time) shows the 'Workout Complete' popup and, after acknowledging, routes straight to /summary -- reproducible even with localStorage/sessionStorage cleared first (ruling out stale test-session cache). Root cause appears to be in the segTotalSec/segments duration computation for this specific catalog entry (workout.tsx lines ~600-636: 'if (segTotalSec > 0 && telemetry.elapsed >= segTotalSec)') -- segTotalSec is likely resolving to a near-zero value for this workout's segment definition. NOT caused by this round's diff (git diff confirms only struggle.ts/onStruggle/coach.py/summary.tsx STRUGGLE_LABEL changed this round; the completion-detection code is untouched). Verified other catalog workouts (e.g. 'Threshold Intervals', workoutId=threshold-intervals-foundation) run normally with correctly-ticking telemetry and no premature completion, so this is isolated to this one catalog item, not a general regression of the live-ride flow.

issues: When a ride ends with too little/no telemetry (needsManual=true path, e.g. a very short session), the Summary header still displays the hardcoded design-mock content from summaryContent (title 'Threshold Climb', date 'Wednesday, 12 May 2025' -- src/lib/summary.ts lines 63-97) rather than the actual just-ridden workout's name and today's date. Confirmed unrelated to this round's Priority 3 diff (summary.ts/SummaryHeader untouched this round); pre-existing mock-data leak in the manual-entry fallback path, low priority since the manual-entry card itself (workout name, save flow) works correctly.

Code review: struggle.ts systemicFatigue() gate -- 15-min longBuf, >=13min data-gate, powerStable (<=8% delta), hrDrift>5%, standalone trigger, 10% ease, REASON_PRIORITY ordering -- all match the Priority 3 spec exactly.

Not a Priority 3 regression (unrelated code path), but worth a quick fix since it blocks that specific catalog item from being ridden at all.

User's own Node-script math verification (1 firing case + 3 negative controls, all correct) is a reasonable substitute given this constraint.
critical_code_review_comments: struggle.ts: systemicFatigue() correctly requires both wearableOn AND trainerOn AND lb.length>=10 before evaluating, avoiding false positives when either sensor is missing.

struggle.ts: the 15-min longBuf is independent of and does not interfere with the existing 10s WINDOW_SEC buffer used for the other struggle signals -- no shared mutable state between the two horizons other than the same push() call.

routes/coach.py: the new hydration instruction branch is placed correctly ahead of the generic 'else' struggle branch and after the preemptive w_prime_low branch, so priority ordering (preemptive > systemic_fatigue > generic) matches struggle.ts's REASON_PRIORITY array (erg_spiral > w_prime_low > systemic_fatigue > hr_near_max > ...).
New CoachCueRequest usage is additive (struggle_reasons=['systemic_fatigue'] is just a new value in an existing list field) -- no schema change needed, confirmed backward compatible by test.

Minor, unrelated to this round: the instant-complete bug on 'Welcome Ride' and the SummaryHeader mock-data leak (see ui_bugs/design_issues) are both pre-existing issues surfaced incidentally during this round's regression pass, not introduced by the Priority 3 diff.
